Campaign brief: You can put an AI agent on the repetitive part of your support inbox and stay the one who decides what is sent — with the safeguards as defaults, and a way to check its answers yourself before anything touches a customer.
events.reader:
Selected audience: Support lead who answers the same forty tickets and has to sell the idea upward.
Situation context (inferred; check applicability): The full-time support person at a 30-40 person company who answers where is my order and what is your return policy forty times a morning, has the answers in documents nobody outside the team reads, no developer to assign, and a genuine fear that an automated reply promises a refund the company does not offer.
events.reader_segment: Support lead who answers the same forty tickets and has to sell the idea upward
events.promise: You can put an AI agent on the repetitive part of your support inbox and stay the one who decides what is sent — with the safeguards as defaults, and a way to check its answers yourself before anything touches a customer.
events.arc: Email 1 removes the reason she will not start: it names the fear (an automated reply promising a refund, or a connected inbox answering the archive) and answers it with defaults rather than promises — human approval is the out-of-the-box setting. Email 2 changes the size of the ask: she does not have to connect a live inbox or find a developer to find out whether it answers her questions correctly; she can upload her own policy document and test it in a browser, seeing per message whether the answer came from her document. Email 1 makes it safe to consider; email 2 makes it cheap to find out. Each stands alone.

emails.job: Get a support lead who considers inbox automation too risky to open a free account and look at the approval queue.
emails.single_idea: An agent can draft the repetitive replies without a single word reaching a customer unapproved — human validation is the default setting, not an option you have to remember to switch on.
emails.objection: If I let an AI answer customers unsupervised, it will eventually promise something we don't offer, and that costs more than the time it saves.
must_not_say: Any plan limit, credit count or execution count — the company's own pricing pages contradict each other on Pro and Free; only $0/$29/$99 and the 1,500 signup credits are safe, and none of them belong in this email
Any promise about order status / 'où est ma commande' questions — answering those needs live tracking data the product evidence does not cover
Anything about the knowledge base, uploaded documents, citing sources or the Playground — email 2 owns that argument
Code, curl, API keys, JSON schemas, IMAP/SMTP ports, webhooks or endpoints — one code-shaped line loses this reader
Security, uptime, SOC 2, GDPR or encryption claims — she is not running a vendor security review at this stage, and the field is ahead of us on that axis
Any customer name, testimonial, logo or usage figure — none exist
Any quantified saving: no hours per week, no percentage of tickets deflected, no response-time figure
Do not claim the agent is accurate or that its drafts will be good — this email is about who decides, not about answer quality
emails.felt_need: Two-thirds of what lands in the shared inbox every morning is the same policy and returns questions, and I retype the answers myself before I can start my actual job. But one automated reply promising a refund we don't offer would cost more than the whole month it saves me.
emails.status_quo: Answering by hand, at audience level — possibly with canned replies in the helpdesk — copying answers that already exist in a returns policy or FAQ document.
emails.why_it_fails: Canned replies save keystrokes, not decisions: someone still has to read every message and pick the answer, so the cost stays proportional to the volume.
emails.mechanism: The agent drafts from the connected inbox, but auto-reply is off by default — the draft lands in an approval queue with status pending_approval, and you review, edit, then send or ignore. Two more defaults shrink the blast radius: senders that look automated (no-reply, mailer-daemon, postmaster) are skipped, and messages older than 24 hours are never touched, so connecting an inbox does not answer the archive.

emails.job: Get a support lead with no developer to sign up and test the agent on her own support document in the Playground, without connecting an inbox.
emails.single_idea: You can find out whether it actually answers your questions — on your own returns policy, in a browser, without a developer and without touching the live inbox.
emails.objection: It is sold as no-code, but everything I can find about it looks like it was written for developers — and I don't have one.
must_not_say: Do not re-argue the approval queue, auto-reply defaults, the 24-hour rule or skipped automated senders — email 1 owns those

Do not promise retrieval quality: no claim that it will answer every question correctly, understand paraphrases, or match a human. The honest move is to invite the test, because nothing in the evidence measures retrieval quality
Do not extend the 'under 2 minutes' figure beyond creating an agent — it does not cover connecting an inbox, a full setup or a rollout
Any plan limit, credit count or execution count — the pricing tables contradict each other; 'gratuit, sans carte bancaire' is the only commercial fact this email may use
Any promise about order status / 'où est ma commande' — not supported
No code, curl, API keys, JSON, IMAP/SMTP ports or endpoint talk, even to say it is optional
Do not position this as replacing the helpdesk or migrating anything — the ask is one document beside what already exists
No customer names, quotes, logos or usage figures — none exist
Do not name or compare competitors, and do not raise speed, breadth, quality or security as axes
emails.felt_need: The answers are all in a PDF and a FAQ nobody outside the team reads. I have no developer to assign this to, so 'try an AI tool' has stayed on my list for months as something I cannot start.
emails.status_quo: The evaluation gets postponed: with no engineering time allocated and no obvious first step, the question of whether an AI could handle the repetitive part stays theoretical.
emails.why_it_fails: A question you cannot test stays an opinion. As long as trying it looks like a project that needs someone technical, it loses every week to the inbox itself.
emails.mechanism: You create the agent from the console — write what it should do, pick a model, no code — and upload your returns policy or shipping FAQ as a document. On each question the agent pulls the relevant passages from your documents automatically; there is no vector database to run. In the Playground you ask it your ten most frequent questions and a database icon appears on every message where it actually used your document, so you can see whether the answer came from your policy or from the model.

events.subject: Aucune réponse ne part sans votre accord
events.preview_text: La réponse automatique est désactivée par défaut — le brouillon attend dans la file d'approbation.
events.body:
Un agent peut rédiger les réponses répétitives de votre boîte support sans qu'un seul mot parte chez un client sans votre accord.

orqAgent est une plateforme sans code pour créer des agents IA. Son agent Email Inbox lit la boîte partagée, prépare un brouillon de réponse — puis s'arrête là.

Les réponses types font gagner des frappes, pas des décisions. Quelqu'un doit encore ouvrir chaque message et choisir la bonne : le coût reste proportionnel au volume.

Ici, la réponse automatique est **désactivée par défaut**. Le brouillon arrive dans la file d'approbation avec le statut pending_approval : vous relisez, vous modifiez si besoin, puis vous envoyez ou vous ignorez.

Deux autres réglages par défaut réduisent la portée. Les expéditeurs qui ressemblent à des robots — no-reply, mailer-daemon, postmaster — sont ignorés, et les messages de plus de **24 heures** ne sont jamais traités.

Connecter une boîte ne répond donc pas à votre archive.

Vous pouvez créer un compte et regarder la file d'approbation avant de connecter quoi que ce soit.

events.body:
Sur une boîte support reliée à un agent, l'envoi automatique est **désactivé par défaut**.

Le brouillon ne part pas : il arrive dans une file d'approbation avec le statut pending_approval. Vous relisez, vous modifiez si besoin, puis vous envoyez ou vous ignorez.

Les réponses types font gagner des frappes, pas des décisions : quelqu'un doit toujours ouvrir chaque message et choisir la bonne. Sur les questions de retour ou de conditions générales, ce coût reste proportionnel au volume.

orqAgent est une plateforme sans code : vous configurez un agent depuis une console, il rédige les brouillons de réponse aux emails entrants, et vous restez celle qui décide de ce qui part.

Deux autres réglages par défaut limitent la portée. Les expéditeurs qui ressemblent à des robots — no-reply, mailer-daemon, postmaster — sont ignorés. Et les messages de plus de **24 heures** ne sont jamais traités : brancher une boîte ne répond pas à l'archive.

Commencez par la partie de la boîte où une erreur ne coûte rien : créez un compte gratuit et regardez la file d'approbation avant de brancher quoi que ce soit.

edits.line: Son agent Email Inbox lit la boîte partagée, prépare un brouillon de réponse — puis s'arrête là.
edits.problem: Nothing on the page says where the draft's content comes from. All three cold readers landed on the same conclusion: if the agent is guessing, the approval queue does not remove a task, it adds one (reading forty wrong drafts instead of typing forty right ones). The email kills the safety objection and accidentally creates a value objection in its place — and the brief's own promise for the campaign is that she stays the one who decides, which only pays if the thing she is deciding on is worth reviewing.
edits.fix: One clause here saying what the draft is written from — the support documents you give it, which is how the company describes the product and is covered by E60 — without any claim that the drafts are accurate or good. That stays inside the brief's exclusion (email 2 still owns the knowledge base, citations and Playground); what is needed here is orientation, not the argument.

edits.line: Vous pouvez créer un compte et regarder la file d'approbation avant de connecter quoi que ce soit.
edits.problem: The ask promises she can inspect the approval queue before connecting an inbox, but no evidence establishes that there is anything to see there without a connected inbox — E102 describes the queue's behaviour once a draft exists. As written, the low-friction step she is being sold is a look at an empty page, and one reader flagged this exact line as one to cut.
edits.fix: Narrow the ask to what a free signup verifiably gives her — the account is free and needs no card (E25) — or restate the inspection so it matches what the product actually shows before an inbox is connected. Keep it to one ask, stated once.

edits.line: Les réponses types font gagner des frappes, pas des décisions. Quelqu'un doit encore ouvrir chaque message et choisir la bonne : le coût reste proportionnel au volume.
edits.problem: This is where the reader who quit stopped, and two of three named it as a line to change. It arrives immediately after the product has been introduced, asserts as fact a workflow she may not have (canned replies in a helpdesk), and explains her own problem back to her — which the audience note explicitly warns against, since she already knows the problem and needs to see it is solvable at all.
edits.fix: Compress this beat to a single line, or cut it and go straight from the product sentence to the defaults. If it stays, it must read as a statement about canned replies in general, not as a claim about how she works today. The reader gets to the ask without this paragraph.

edits.line: Un agent peut rédiger les réponses répétitives de votre boîte support sans qu'un seul mot parte chez un client sans votre accord.
edits.problem: The opening line carries the whole idea but stacks two 'sans' in one sentence and reads as translated rather than written; 'parte chez un client' is off in French. The house voice is short declarative sentences, often paired — a claim then a literal follow-up — not one long subordinated clause.
edits.fix: Split it into the two beats it already contains: what the agent does, then what does not happen without her. Keep the same claim; fix the grammar and the rhythm.

edits.line: Connecter une boîte ne répond donc pas à votre archive.
edits.problem: The 'donc' points back at a paragraph that listed two defaults, but the conclusion only follows from the 24-hour rule; a reader briefly has to work out which of the two it attaches to.
edits.fix: Attach the conclusion to the 24-hour default explicitly, or fold it into that clause so the inference is not left to the reader.

events.preview_text: L'agent rédige à partir de vos documents support ; l'envoi automatique est désactivé par défaut.
events.body:
Relier un agent à votre boîte support, ce n'est pas lui donner le droit de parler à vos clients.

orqAgent est une plateforme sans code pour créer des agents IA. Son agent Email Inbox lit la boîte partagée et rédige un brouillon de réponse à partir des documents support que vous lui donnez — puis il s'arrête là.

L'envoi automatique est **désactivé par défaut**. Le brouillon arrive dans la file d'approbation avec le statut pending_approval : vous relisez, vous modifiez si besoin, puis vous envoyez ou vous ignorez.

Deux autres réglages par défaut limitent la portée. Les expéditeurs qui ressemblent à des robots — no-reply, mailer-daemon, postmaster — sont ignorés, et les messages de plus de 24 heures ne sont jamais traités.

Relier une boîte ne répond donc pas à votre archive.

Le compte est gratuit et ne demande pas de carte bancaire. Vous créez l'agent et vous réglez son comportement avant de relier quoi que ce soit.

events.body:
Relier une boîte support à un agent, on imagine d'abord la vague.

Des centaines de réponses parties d'un coup, dont une qui promet un remboursement que vous ne faites pas. Ce n'est pas ce qui se passe.

Les messages de plus de **24 heures** sont ignorés — relier une boîte ne répond jamais à votre archive. Les expéditeurs automatiques, no-reply ou mailer-daemon, sont écartés eux aussi.

Reste la part répétitive : les mêmes questions de retours et de politique commerciale, dont la réponse ne change pas d'un mois à l'autre. Les réponses enregistrées font gagner des frappes, pas des décisions — il faut encore lire chaque message et choisir la bonne.

orqAgent est une plateforme sans code pour créer des agents IA depuis une console. Sur une boîte support, l'envoi automatique est **désactivé par défaut** : le brouillon arrive dans une file d'approbation, vous le relisez, vous le modifiez, puis Envoyer ou Ignorer.

Le compte est gratuit, sans carte bancaire. Vous pouvez ouvrir la console et regarder cette file d'approbation avant de relier la moindre boîte.
events.postscript: Aucun développeur n'est nécessaire : tout se configure depuis la console.
